brief: A Market Ear chart compilation arguing that growth, capex, commodities, yields and positioning are all stretched to extremes at once. S&P 500 2026 earnings are forecast to grow 34%, more than double the 15% growth expected earlier this year, driven by an AI boom rather than a post-recession rebound. Consensus hyperscaler capex has risen from under $300bn to $940bn, pushing tech to a record 25% share of global profits even as margins sit at a structural-plus-cyclical high the piece flags as a sustainability question. The boom is not US-only: EM earnings growth is running at 72% y/y, Korea buybacks are climbing toward unprecedented levels, and Europe's economic surprise index is at multi-year highs. Cost-side extremes are appearing too: crack spreads, gasoline, diesel and electricity prices are all at records, the 10-year Treasury yield closed at its highest since 2023, and China has bought gold for 22 straight months. USD and vol-control positioning are crowded, and GS expects a record $700bn of 2026 equity issuance. The note makes no directional call of its own. It argues the convergence itself is what is abnormal.
